text:
maya: Heads-up — overnight dashboard shows batch_utilization drop on eu-west nodes around 03:10 UTC, token/sec down ~22% but request latency unchanged. spotted via the batcher-summary panel :eyes:
liam: weird, same commit? any deploys?
sanjay: no deploys during that window, infra-bot alerted about a KV miss spike at 03:09 UTC (:warning:). attaching the query I ran below.
olivia: can you paste graphs or the raw query? want to check queue depth + sample rate.
maya: here's the quick promql I used — it shows token/sec per pod and batch_utilization: ```
sum by(pod) (rate(batcher_tokens_produced_total[1m])) / ignoring(pod) group_left sum by(pod) (batcher_max_tokens_capacity)
```
liam: that looks right. also check batch formation rate and microbatch counts: ```sum(rate(batcher_batches_created_total[1m]))```
rafael: infra-bot dump: "KV cache miss rate increased from 2.1% to 8.7% between 03:05-03:12". suspect kvcache eviction churn due to an unusual prefix distribution from a customer load test.
maya: load test? who ran that? @sanjay any known spike?
sanjay: ops ran a synthetic throughput test hitting prompt_prefix=X pattern at 03:02-03:08, might have very different length distribution causing kernel fallback and increasing per-token work.
olivia: if kernel selection changed (float16->int8 path) we'd see CPU/GPU ripple — did kernel_choice metric flip?
rafael: quick check: `batcher_kernel_path_switches_total{reason="precision_fallback"}` shows +14 in same window on eu-west pods.
liam: ok that ties together: more kernel fallbacks + KV misses -> smaller batches (more token overhead) -> token/sec drop. need telemetry to stitch these signals in one pane.
maya: proposal: make a single "batching health" dashboard with the following panels: batch_utilization, avg_microbatch_size, queue_depth_p50/p95, tokens_per_sec, kvcache_hit_ratio, kernel_path_switches, and kernel_latency_percentiles. also correlate with sampling of request prompt_length distribution.
sanjay: agree. two immediate asks: 1) increase sampling for prompt-prefix telemetry from 1% -> 5% for 10 minutes to verify prefix distribution; 2) add a derived metric: effective_tokens_per_batch = tokens_produced / batches_created.
olivia: small PR to metrics exporter for derived metric is straightforward. I'll draft it and post.
rafael: On queue policy side, there's a knob `max_formation_delay_ms`. If kvcache storms reduce batchable tokens, the broker should lengthen formation window by ~30ms to avoid underfilled batches. Suggest a short experiment on canary.
liam: let's not change production default until we can see the dashboard. do the sampling + derived metric, build dashboard, then run a canary tweak for 2 hours.
maya: plan: olivia -> metrics PR (ETA 2h), samplings change by sanjay in infra (ETA 15m), then I'll assemble the dashboard and run correlation queries. canary tweak after we confirm.
sanjay: infra change done: sampling now 5% (rolled back to 1% at 03:27 for now but prometheus scraped samples during the window). infra-bot: "sampling-change: 1%->5% by sanjay at 03:17 UTC"
olivia: PR opened: exporters/batcher_metrics: add effective_tokens_per_batch gauge + kernel_path_switch_count. link: https://git.internal/r/exp/1234 (cc @maya)
rafael: I'll prepare a small canary plan: target two pods in eu-west, set `max_formation_delay_ms += 30`, monitor effective_tokens_per_batch and p95 latency for 30m. revert on increased latency.
liam: also add alert rule: if batch_utilization drops >15% vs 30m baseline and kvcache_hit_ratio < 94% -> page oncall.
maya: thanks all. follow-ups: olivia to post PR link, maya to post dashboard JSON, rafael to run canary once metrics are populated. keep this thread for rollup. :thumbsup:
